statement: Positive Euler exponents, reciprocal functional equation, rational local polynomials and alternating self-duality do not supply the geometric-monodromy pole control required by DeligneI(3.2). The explicit A=[[2,1],[1,3]] yields both a formal positive zeta with off-circle roots and a genuine constant-arithmetic lisse-sheaf test.
compatible_assumptions: Formal zeta satisfies the listed rationality/positivity/symmetry axioms. For ℓ≠5 the sheaf has geometric Frobenius A, pairing to Qℓ(−1), and rational local determinants. Its geometric monodromy is trivial, so the open-Sp hypothesis is expressly NOT satisfied.
new_claim_suggested: Use this construction as a reusable mandatory negative control for proposals that infer purity from the weaker axioms. No literature novelty is asserted.
already_proved: All-degree nonnegative Euler exponents by primitive-orbit injection; alternating multiplier5; continuous lisse-sheaf realization and explicit tensor L-function poles.
conjectural: Whether any particular number-field proposal has stronger axioms sufficient to evade this obstruction remains unassessed.
next_step: Review the all-degree proof independently and test candidate trace/spectral models against precisely the same list of axioms.
potential_counterexamples: A model with actual geometric open-Sp monodromy or a positive invariant metric is outside this counterexample's hypotheses; do not overextend the obstruction.
tests: experiments/code/geometry_round2_exact.py: exact trace recurrence, first80 Euler exponents and cyclic-label uniqueness through period8; the all-n proof is in frontiers/geometry_round2.md.
significance: Separates geometric purity from several tempting but insufficient algebraic and analytic substitutes.
difficulty: Elementary construction; applying it to a proposed infinite-dimensional number-field model requires exact axiom matching.
status: Explicit proof plus independent parent check; no external novelty review.

statement: The inspected even-tensor Euler-product proof needs sublinear excess weight on geometric coinvariants, rather than the whole open-Sp hypothesis as a black box. Coinvariant bounds q^(kβ+Ck), Ck=o(k), give local |α|≤q_x^(β/2+(Ck+1)/(2k)); alternating duality supplies equality.
compatible_assumptions: Affine open U0⊂P1/Fq; lisse Qℓ-sheaf, ℓ≠char Fq; perfect alternating pairing to Qℓ(−β); rational local characteristic polynomials; algebraic Frobenius coinvariant eigenvalues with all-conjugate bound for arbitrarily large k. These are explicit hypotheses, not claimed available for classical zeta.
new_claim_suggested: Derived sufficient-condition lemma THM-G013: replace exact Sp-invariant Tate pole control by asymptotically Tate even-tensor coinvariants.
already_proved: Deligne's coefficient positivity, cohomological formula and power argument; source-grounded reconstruction of the conditional implication supplied.
conjectural: No classical-number-field realization or sublinear tensor-degree bound is known from this campaign. Separate review of the derived lemma remains pending.
next_step: Independently check coefficient-field descent, local-factor radius inequality, Hc2 coinvariant identification and all-complex-conjugate quantifiers; then test one non-Sp monodromy family.
potential_counterexamples: The constant arithmetic A-sheaf fails the sublinear bound: α+^(2k) produces excess weight linear in k. Bounds with Ck proportional to k do not force purity.
tests: Symbolic exponent/logarithm calculation; explicit A tensor eigenvalue growth; no numerical observation substitutes for the limiting proof.
significance: Makes the genuinely needed quantitative pole-control input explicit and supplies a sharper target than a vague Frobenius analogy.
difficulty: Small derived lemma moderate; constructing useful nontrivial geometric or number-field examples is high difficulty.
status: Derived lemma under independent review; not assigned literature novelty.

statement: WeilII §2 applies Hadamard–de la Vallée-Poussin/Mertens positivity to get wq(α)<β+2 on curve Hc1, then geometric product/vanishing-cycle iteration sharpens to the optimal weight bound via errors2^(−k).
compatible_assumptions: Smooth curve over Fq, lisse iota-pure sheaf, chosen iota and real weight β. Weight-zero normalization uses twisting; the full proof requires its monodromy and vanishing-cycle hypotheses.
new_claim_suggested: For future reverse transfers to analytic number theory, identify an actual contraction of localization error in addition to a positivity inequality.
already_proved: Historical transfer explicitly described in WeilII introduction pp139–141 and §2; precise strict bound(2.2.10) and iterative estimate(3.2.4) inspected in the primary source.
conjectural: A comparable contraction mechanism for a classical-zeta analytic family is not supplied.
next_step: Fully reconstruct the contraction for one explicit sheaf family, preserving the strict initial bound and integer-weight step, before proposing an analytic analogue.
potential_counterexamples: Coefficient positivity alone passes the A countermodel and does not provide error contraction; merely reusing a trigonometric positivity polynomial is insufficient.
tests: Exact identity3+4cosθ+cos2θ=2(1+cosθ)^2≥0 is a small local check; it does not verify the complete geometric argument.
significance: Preserves a mathematically concrete analytic-to-geometric transfer and identifies the extra ingredient needed for its reversal.
difficulty: Full source reconstruction substantial; any new reverse transfer very high difficulty.
status: Documented established relationship; not a novel literature discovery; full technical reconstruction pending.
